insights.insight: Ad tech charges $5–$150 CPA for modeled attribution; this protocol settles verified purchase confirmation at roughly $0.10 per receipt — a 50–200x cost delta that reflects the difference between inferring intent and proving a transaction occurred.

With Chrome completing cookie deprecation and fingerprinting increasingly blocked, the industry has no cross-ecosystem, identity-free purchase signal at scale — verified receipts are structurally positioned to fill that gap, not incrementally improve on existing solutions.

Amazon, Walmart, and every major retailer each hold a closed fragment of purchase reality; none can see across ecosystems, meaning the first queryable aggregate of cross-channel verified spend data carries intelligence that no single first-party dataset can replicate.

The first Shopify brand appeared in the verified receipt pool at Heartbeat #132 — after 130+ cycles of physical retail only — signaling that the data window now spans both in-store and online purchase behavior, a prerequisite for any meaningful omnichannel attribution use case.

19 active metro and non-metro markets with burst-quiet-burst expansion patterns across both coasts and the upper Midwest suggest network-effect-driven adoption rather than paid distribution — the signal base is growing without the acquisition cost that typically inflates data provider economics.

Only 3.3% of receipt tokens have been claimed via Lightning Network payouts, meaning the incentive layer is not yet clearing at scale; brands evaluating this as a data source should treat current volume as early-adopter signal, not representative panel coverage.
